measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: Neither 'gd-tools coverage show' nor 'gd-tools coverage report' checks plan.json's own recorded source_hash against the actual current file on disk before presenting or writing results. A stale coverage.json/plan.json pair from before a source change is read and reported exactly as if it were fresh -- there is no 'stale' or 'hash mismatch' diagnostic of any kind in either command's output. This is a genuine negative finding, not a null result: gd-tools DOES compute and store a source_hash per file in plan.json (confirmed present and correct), it simply never uses it as a staleness check on the read path, only (presumably) on the write path during an actual test run.

notes: This is the sharper, real-tool-confirmed counterpart to pilot/harness/comparator.py's own stale-report handling (compare()'s stale_files/oracle_stale_files distinction, tested synthetically in self_test.py's test_stale_report_detected and test_oracle_stale_source_detected) -- the harness itself would correctly flag this exact scenario as stale if fed through compare(), but gd-tools' own CLI has no equivalent self-check and will happily hand a caller (or a CI step, or a human running 'gd-tools coverage show' after editing a file and forgetting to re-run tests) a number for source that no longer exists in that form. Any adapter or harness wrapper built on top of gd-tools' CLI output cannot rely on gd-tools itself to catch this -- it must independently verify the plan's recorded source_hash against the current file before trusting a 'coverage show'/'coverage report' result, exactly the check pilot/harness/comparator.py already performs.
